sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "I will be sanctified" involves an arousal from below upward, followed by two types of drawing down from above through Torah and mitzvos.

translations.translation: "And I will be sanctified amidst the children of Israel; I am the L-rd who sanctifies you."
And the Alter Rebbe explains in Likkutei Torah, the discourse beginning with the word "Zeh,"
that "And I will be sanctified amidst the children of Israel"
(the revelation of His holiness within the heart
of Israel)
is in a manner of from below to above,
that the heart of Israel burns like fiery flames to be included in His holiness,
and through this, afterward is drawn "I am the L-rd who sanctifies you,"
the drawing down of His holiness from above to below.
And in this itself
(in the drawing down from above to below)
there are two matters,
the drawing down through Torah and the drawing down through mitzvos.
For the drawing down that is through Torah is in the inwardness of the worlds
(in spirituality),
and in order for the drawing down to be in the externality of the worlds
(in physicality),
it is through the performance of mitzvos.
And this is the meaning of what is said, "Holy, holy, holy,"
that the first "holy" is an elevation from below to above,
and the second and third "holy" are drawings down from above to below,
through Torah and through mitzvos.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the three "holies" correspond to three levels of Kesser, and the difference in their mode of revelation stems from their distinct levels.

translations.translation: And he continues in
(the explanation of)
the maamar,
that the three times "holy" are three levels.
The first "holy" is Kesser
(which is above Chochmah),
the second "holy" is the Kesser of Zeir Anpin,
and the third "holy" is the Kesser of Malchus.
And one can explain this based on what is known,
that "holy"
(in general)
refers to the Surrounding Light, which is holy and separate from the chain of descent.
Therefore, the primary concept of "holy"
(the first "holy")
is in Kesser, which is above Chochmah
(for Chochmah is the beginning of the chain of descent).
And that which even the Kesser of Zeir Anpin and the Kesser of Malchus are called by the name "holy,"
is
because the descent of the Kessarim is not like the descent of cause and effect, where the effect is a different entity from the cause,
but rather,
all the Kessarim are one essence,
and even after the descent of the Kesser to become the Kesser of Zeir Anpin or of Malchus,
it is in its essence as it was before
(the Kesser that is above Chochmah).
And one could say,
that this which is explained in the maamar, that the three times "holy" are distinct in their level
(that the first "holy" is the Kesser above Chochmah,
and the second and third "holy" are the Kesser of Zeir Anpin and of Malchus),
is also an explanation of the difference in their manner
(that the first "holy" is in a manner of from below to above, and the second and third "holy" are in a manner of from above to below).
For the Surrounding [Light]
(Kesser)
itself,
since it is completely holy and separate,
its revelation in a person is in a manner that he recognizes and feels that this is a matter that is wondrous and separate from him,
and therefore he yearns to go out of his existence and be included in that wondrous matter,
and when the Surrounding [Light] descends to become the Kesser of Zeir Anpin or of Malchus,
then its revelation is in a manner that it is drawn downward.
And likewise, regarding the second and third "holy,"
the difference in the manner of their drawing down is because they are distinct in their level.
For the second "holy,"
since its descent is that it becomes the Kesser of Zeir Anpin
(for Zeir Anpin is the end of Atzilus),
its drawing down is
(only)
in the inwardness of the worlds
(through Torah),
and the third "holy,"
which descends to become the Kesser of Malchus
(for Malchus is the root of the created beings),
its drawing down is
(also)
in the externality of the worlds
(through the performance of mitzvos).
